issues.title: Ablation-timed breakdown of radix agg sink per-group cost, then fix the top component
issues.hypothesis: New R4 measurements (dbe-tool sql, hot, 8 threads): SELECT max(s) FROM (SELECT l_orderkey k, sum(l_quantity) s FROM lineitem GROUP BY k) = 455 ms (15M groups). The same with k = l_orderkey//64 (~230K groups, same 60M rows, same clustering) = 220 ms, and //4 (~3.75M groups) = 284 ms. A plain scan with the //64 expression = 115 ms. So the per-row agg path costs ~105 ms wall, and the per-GROUP cost is ~235 ms wall at 15M groups (~125 ns CPU/group, linear in group count). Single-threaded: //64 1.33 s vs full 5.18 s => ~257 ns/group. Three blind attempts at parts of this cost found nothing: E0001 probes (-13% CPU, ~0 wall), E0002 finalize re-materialization (0), E0003 unpartitioned staging (0). We are guessing component by component at 1 round each. One ablation round that times each sink sub-step on the 15M-group query will show which component holds the ~125 ns/group, and then allow a targeted fix in the same round.
issues.plan: Step 1 (measurement, temporary code, never committed): in a scratch build, time the isolated query above (3+ hot runs each via dbe-tool sql; results may be wrong during ablation, which is fine because only timing matters) with each of these removed in turn: (a) RowOperations::InitializeStates in FindOrCreateGroupsInternal (aggregate_hashtable.cpp ~:766); (b) the UpdateAggregates call in GroupedAggregateHashTable::AddChunk (aggregate_hashtable.cpp ~:519 onward); (c) the Abandon()+MaybeRepartition block in RadixPartitionedHashTable::Sink (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp :578-600), by forcing one big local HT instead (e.g. local_sink_capacity = 1<<22 after adaptation), which also tests 'fewer abandons'; (d) the hll.Update path (enable_hll), which only runs for the first 1M rows, as a sanity check; (e) the RadixHTLocalSourceState::Finalize/Scan work, by making GetData emit nothing once Finalize is done. Also compare with skip_lookups forced on (pure append, no probe) to separate probe from materialization. Record wall per variant in the ledger notes. Step 2 (real change): if (c) gives >=8%, implement a generality-safe capacity rule in DecideAdaptation (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424): when dedup is already near the HLL estimate (potential_increase_rate ~1) and the cardinality is high, grow local_sink_capacity up to an L2/L3-sized bound to cut abandon and repartition frequency. If (a) or (b) dominates, look for a per-call overhead fix in RowOperations::InitializeStates or AggregateExecutor scatter (e.g. a fast path for a single fixed-size state with a trivial initialize). If (e) dominates, revisit the source scan/finalize path. If nothing exceeds 8%, stop after step 1 and report the full table. Either result is useful.
issues.expected_gain: q18: 0-15%. The measurement alone decides rounds 5-6. A step-2 fix that targets the dominant per-group component could reach 10-15% because the per-group cost is ~50% of the subquery aggregate.
issues.generality: Every high-cardinality parallel hash aggregate (GROUP BY on a near-unique key, DISTINCT, IN/EXISTS subqueries with GROUP BY HAVING). A capacity-rule change could hurt low-dedup random-key aggregates if the HT outgrows cache, so bound it by L2/L3 size and gate it on the measured dedup ratio.
issues.risk: Low for step 1 (temporary). Medium for step 2, depending on which fix. The memory interplay with external aggregation must be kept: never grow capacity when gstate.external.

dispatch: Ablation-timed breakdown of radix agg sink per-group cost, then fix the top component
output.memory:
## Memory (planner, q18 specialisation run)

### Workload facts (q18 only visible template; baseline ~610-670 ms hot, 8 threads)
- Plan: IN-subquery `GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING sum(l_quantity) > X` over all of lineitem (60M rows -> 15M groups -> ~111 after HAVING).
  HASH_GROUP_BY = 4.6-5.0s CPU. Outer part: lineitem scan 0.17s + probe join 0.26s (60M rows vs 111-row build), orders/customer joins ~0.3s each.
- Group key arrives compressed as UINTEGER (compressed materialization), fixed-width. sum_no_overflow(decimal) -> SumState<int64_t> (int64 state, not hugeint).
- lineitem is clustered on the key (~4 equal keys per run) -> thread-local HTs dedupe almost fully; finalize sees ~6 dups/117K.

### Key measurements (via dbe-tool sql; multiple ;-separated statements in one call work, the first run is cold; ±15% noise)
- Isolated subquery agg ~455 ms wall of q18's ~630. Plain lineitem scan (max(l_orderkey),sum(l_quantity)) ~71 ms; with l_orderkey//64 expr 115 ms.
- R4 per-row vs per-group split (same 60M rows, same clustering): GROUP BY l_orderkey//64 (~230K groups) 220 ms; //4 (~3.75M groups) 284 ms;
  full key (15M) 455 ms => per-group cost ~125 ns CPU at 8t, linear in groups; per-row agg cost ~14 ns CPU.
  threads=1: //64 1.33 s, full 5.18 s => ~257 ns/group (1-2 threads use the grow strategy, a different path).
- R3: `GROUP BY ... LIMIT 1` ~410 ms vs full ~440 => sink dominates; finalize ~30-50 ms.
- Thread scaling: 4t 870 ms, 8t 455, 16t 350 => CPU-bound.
- allocator_flush_threshold / bulk_dealloc threshold = 8GB, block_allocator_memory: no effect.
- count(*) without the sum ~330 ms vs ~440 with it.

### Join-filter finding (R3, not worth pursuing)
- Join filter pushdown can't pass through __internal_compress_integral projections; disabling compressed_materialization lets
  filters reach the scan but q18 wall is unchanged. => Low-value direction.

### Codebase facts
- Radix sink: Sink() (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:548) -> ht.AddChunk (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:519) -> FindOrCreateGroupsInternal (:641).
  New groups go to unpartitioned_data (staging) if radix_bits>=3 && new/partitions<=4 (:756); Abandon() repartitions staging.
  Sink capacity 32768 (>2 threads) -> abandon every ~16K groups (Sink :578-600).
- DecideAdaptation (:424): SkipLookups if HLL unique >95%; grows capacity only if dedup could improve 2x; ADAPTIVITY_THRESHOLD 1M rows.
- MaybeRepartition (:479): radix bits 3 -> +2 steps -> max 8 (MAXIMUM_FINAL_SINK_RADIX_BITS), row-width adjusted; GetThreadLimit =
  reservation/threads*0.8; over-limit path grabs a lock and doubles the reservation (log-many times, probably cheap).
- Source finalize: RadixHTLocalSourceState::Finalize builds a new HT per partition + Combine.
- Compressed materialization runs inside statistics propagation, before JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN.
- Settings: perfect_ht_threshold=12, memory_limit 12.2GiB, disabled_optimizers works.
- dbe-tool has no perf; only build/bench/profile/sql. Ablation (temporarily removing a step and timing) is the way to break down costs.

### Directions
- R1 E0001 run-collapse: retired (probes not the bottleneck).
- R2 E0002 in-place finalize: retired, +5%.
- R3 E0003 skip staging for fixed-width layouts: retired, +0.5%.
- R4 dispatched: ablation breakdown of sink per-group cost (InitializeStates / UpdateAggregates / abandon+repartition / source),
  then fix the top component (pre-planned: bigger local capacity when dedup is already near-HLL; init/scatter fast path).
  Read its ablation table before choosing R5. If no component is >8%, consider: smaller row layout (the stored hash
  is recomputable for small keys, high risk), or a key-range direct-index aggregate for dense int keys with lazily allocated pages
  (the q13 analog in auto-memory gave -18.6%, but the q18 key range is ~4x the groups, ~26 bits at SF10, so it needs page-lazy
  thread-local arrays plus a striped combine; 2-round effort, memory-guard by stats range).
- Backlog: 'Instrument and fix radix sink partition growth' is mostly superseded by the R4 ablation (repartitions happen early when
  data is small, so they are likely cheap).
